headline: Tax rate vote held over; $3.5 million in new growth weighed for Burncoat High School fund.
summary: The chief financial officer estimated the city's share of the new Burncoat High School would be $325 million of a $650 million cost. The tax vote is set for next week, with options to put all, half, or $2.5 million of the $3.5 million in new growth into the school fund. A draft public camping ordinance was advertised, and a rodeo ordinance was filed 8-3 instead of going to committee.

Closed the hearing on items 7A and 7B and adopted them.

discussion: Tax rate and Burncoat fund: Members weighed putting all, half, or $2.5 million of the $3.5 million in new growth into the new high school fund, or lowering the tax levy instead. The chief financial officer said each $1 million change is about $13 a year for the average single-family home at the lowest residential rate.

Rodeo ordinance at DCU Center: Public speakers urged a ban on flank straps and electric prods over animal pain and public safety. Others said the events bring visitors and spending to the city, and the city manager said research on flank straps is mixed.

Homeless camping ordinance: Speakers said shelters were full and asked for more beds before enforcement. The commissioner said 81 beds would be available starting December 1st, with a contingency plan for January and February.

Drones for bikes and e-bikes: Members and speakers debated using drones to locate groups of riders who weave through traffic. Speakers raised privacy concerns, and the city manager said any policy would need review.

Private plow contractor rates: Some members said the $115 an hour rate for pickup-truck plows did not change and asked for an increase. The commissioner said it was too early to know how many contractors had signed up.
